## Slide 006 — "Less Than Equal Constraints"

**Header:** Red title "Less Than Equal Constraints" centered; yellow rounded badge with slide number **6** at top-right. The content sits inside a white panel framed by a thin red border, with three horizontally-bordered section boxes.

---

### Box 1 — 3 constraints (red label, italic)
$$x_1 \le z_1,\quad x_2 \le z_2,\quad x_3 \le z_3 \;\Longrightarrow$$
$$
\begin{bmatrix}1&0&0\\0&1&0\\0&0&1\end{bmatrix}
\begin{bmatrix}x_1\\x_2\\x_3\end{bmatrix}
\le
\begin{bmatrix}z_1\\z_2\\z_3\end{bmatrix}
$$
Green implication arrow (⇒) at left. At right: a pink/red rounded callout reading **$Gx \le h$** in red bold.

---

### Box 2 — Greater-than converted
$$x_1 \ge z_1,\quad x_2 \ge z_2,\quad x_3 \ge z_3 \;\Longrightarrow$$
$$
\begin{bmatrix}-1&0&0\\0&-1&0\\0&0&-1\end{bmatrix}
\begin{bmatrix}x_1\\x_2\\x_3\end{bmatrix}
\le
\begin{bmatrix}-z_1\\-z_2\\-z_3\end{bmatrix}
$$
Right side shows a pale-yellow rounded "**Convert**" panel:
> Convert
> $x_1 \ge z_1,\; x_2 \ge z_2,\; x_3 \ge z_3$
> **to**
> $-x_1 \le -z_1,\; -x_2 \le -z_2,\; -x_3 \le -z_3$

---

### Box 3 — 6 constraints, 3 variables (label in red)
$$y_1 \le x_1 \le z_1,\quad y_2 \le x_2 \le z_2,\quad y_3 \le x_3 \le z_3 \;\Longrightarrow$$
$$
\underbrace{\begin{bmatrix}-1&0&0\\0&-1&0\\0&0&-1\\1&0&0\\0&1&0\\0&0&1\end{bmatrix}}_{6\times 3}
\begin{bmatrix}x_1\\x_2\\x_3\end{bmatrix}
\le
\begin{bmatrix}-y_1\\-y_2\\-y_3\\z_1\\z_2\\z_3\end{bmatrix}
$$
(with the "$6\times3$" annotation in small red type beside the matrix). At right: pink rounded callout **$G\underline{x} \le h$** (with $x$ underlined).

---

**Visual style notes:** Red section borders, red bold headings and inequalities, black matrices, blue RHS entries in boxes 1–2, green "⇒" arrows, yellow "Convert" box with red italic heading. The bottom of the frame overlaps a black band (letterbox edge of the capture).

**Takeaway:** Every constraint set — including one-sided "≥" and two-sided bounds — is expressed in the standard form **$Gx \le h$**, with $G$ holding the sign/direction encoding and $h$ the bound vector.
